limits: Statements: fetched for the 160 strongest of 177 shares in an upward trend, to keep the run short.
Statements: stopped after 128 of 160 shares (time budget).
Insiders and holders: looked up for the best 40 of 104, because those two sites are small and block heavy use.
European companies are covered only through their US listings. They file no US insider forms and their statements give no per-share value here, so they can pass five checks at most.
The list is the 240 largest US and 60 largest European names by market value that trade at least 20 million dollars a day; smaller companies are not screened.

method: Stage 1: two years of daily prices for every share on the list (trend and momentum). Stage 2: company statements and the last earnings report for the shares above their 200-day average (value, quality, earnings drift). Stage 3: insider trades and well-known holders for those passing at least three of the first five checks. A share qualifies with five of seven, and the trend check must be one of them.
sources: Nasdaq (share list, statements, earnings), CNBC (prices), OpenInsider (insider trades), Dataroma (well-known holders).
